meta.title: process-category effect conditional on scale and method
meta.process_label_contrast: positive value = Glacial rate HIGHER than Nonglacial (dex)

filters.logER: rows with Erosion rate (mm/yr) > 0 (427/427 glacial, 6284/6288 nonglacial)
filters.matched: each glacial row with finite logER+logTI matched to k=5 nearest nonglacial neighbours on |dlogTI| within the same Methodology (k reduced to n available if fewer)
filters.regression: complete cases on logER, logTI, Process, Methodology

verification.exhumation_note: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, NOT "exactly". ER(mm/yr)*TI(yr)/1000 (proper m conversion) equals the column labelled "Exhumation (m)" within 1% for 48/92 rows (within 0.1%: 28); median ratio 1.002004. The un-converted product ER*TI equals the column directly for 0/92 rows. A MINORITY subset (7/92) has the column numerically equal to the RAW unconverted mm product, i.e. those rows carry a genuine mm-as-m unit error (all are nonglacial Rd 7/11 nonglacial rows). The remaining rows fail both identities because rate/interval were independently rounded before deposition. Net: the column is mostly (but not exactly) ER*TI in metres, with a small mm-contaminated subset.

alternative_matchers.label: ALL pooled across methods, logTI only

volumetric_sign_conflict_diagnosis.note: The nonglacial Volumetric logTI distribution is strongly bimodal (median 0.70 dex with a wide IQR); the glacial one is unimodal at ~1.65 dex. A single linear logTI slope therefore cannot be a common adjustment, and the regression-adjusted contrast is not comparable to the matched contrast.

within_method_common_support.note: NO logTI common support at the 5-95% level

well_supported_fine_cells.interpretation: Only two Methodology x logTI-decile cells contain >=3 glacial and >=20 nonglacial rows: Volumetric / logTI in (-2.563, 0.699] (n_glacial=68, n_nonglacial=2579, diff=+1.079 dex) and Cosmogenic detrital / logTI in (0.699, 3.083] (n_glacial=4, n_nonglacial=487, diff=+0.168 dex). The widely quoted Volumetric contrast is therefore dominated by a single cell holding 2579 of the 2583 nonglacial Volumetric rows. Broadening the cell set to >=2 glacial rows drops the glacial-weighted within-cell contrast to 0.610 dex over 6 cells (93 glacial rows); only the two large cells reach 1.03-1.08 dex. The scale-conditional process contrast is therefore not stable: it ranges from ~0.2 to ~2.1 dex across cells, and shrinks as more (smaller) cells are admitted.

pooled_joint_control_model.note: matched-difference model: intercept = process effect net of within-pair imbalance in controls

fully_adjusted_ols.note: complete cases on logA/logS/logP/absLat; coefficient = Nonglacial minus Glacial in dex. This is an out-of-support extrapolation: it forces a common control slope across the two very different samples.

attenuation_summary.note: the fully adjusted OLS overshoots past zero (sign reversal) because it extrapolates a common control slope across samples with disjoint latitude/precipitation support.
